subject.title: MEDIA: directive with absolute local paths outside default media roots silently fails (Telegram)

question: Should #100292 be scoped to Telegram's blocked-MEDIA diagnostics while #47002/#47856/#52951 own root expansion, or should this issue define a new public Telegram/media root config contract?
rationale: Both outcomes are plausible, but choosing whether to add a config surface or keep this as a diagnostics-only issue changes a security-sensitive host file-read boundary.

options.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots Elsewhere
options.body: Keep this issue open for clearer Telegram/user-visible blocked-media failures and leave durable root expansion to #47002/#47856 or the accepted tools.fs.roots design.

options.title: Make This the Telegram Root Contract
options.body: Use this issue to specify and implement a Telegram-visible media root configuration path with security review and upgrade documentation.

options.title: Close Into Broad FS Roots
options.body: Close this only after #52951 or a successor lands and proves Telegram reply MEDIA paths use the new policy without weakening sandbox/default behavior.

recommendation.title: Diagnostics Here, Roots Elsewhere
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for clearer Telegram/user-visible blocked-media failures and leave durable root expansion to #47002/#47856 or the accepted tools.fs.roots design.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent outbound media access commits make this the closest current owner signal for deciding whether diagnostics or root expansion belongs in this path.
